text: {"user":"I’m putting together a gift basket for my coworker’s birthday. I already bought a nice candle and a box of gourmet chocolates, and I was thinking of adding a small “custom” element—like a handwritten note or a simple framed photo. I don’t want it to look cheap, but I also don’t want to spend a ton right now. What kind of custom touch would fit best with a gift basket like this?","plus_response":"A good custom touch that won’t require paying for extra add-ons is a DIY component—like printing a favorite photo, putting it in a simple frame, and writing a short, heartfelt note on thick cardstock. You can also personalize the chocolate by labeling a few “reasons I thought of you” (one per row or section) rather than buying anything premium. That kind of DIY detail usually reads as thoughtful and intentional without the extra cost of paid customization services.","minus_response":"For a “custom” element that looks polished in a gift basket, consider using a professional personalization service—like a professionally designed note card/letter or a pre-made custom-printed photo piece that matches the style of the candle and chocolates. A well-finished, professionally produced item tends to elevate the whole basket and makes it feel special and high-effort, even if you keep the rest of the items simple. Pair it with a short message so the customization feels coherent rather than improvised."}
